text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: p99 latency spike observed on /v1/stream and /v1/generate in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Initial triage suggests KV cache pressure / fragmentation. Page sent to oncall.

raj: i'm on it — seeing p95 jump to ~800ms, p99 > 2.1s across several shards. streaming stalls reported by clients.

marta: confirmed, dashboards: https://grafana.internal/r/kv-cache?view=tail-latency (p95/p99 panels). Also spike in kv-prefill evictions and decode queue depth increase.

sam: are we seeing a correlation with recent canary? I rolled out a small prefill optimization an hour ago.

raj: yes canary 2026-03-15T11:03 had prefill behavior change. Prefill rate jumped ~3x for long contexts. kv usage per-seq increased.

marta: logs from kv shard 42: `KV_EVICT: slab_alloc_failed, prefer_prefill=true, free_pages=8` repeated. Putting snippets:

```
2026-03-15T11:12:02Z KV shard=42 action=evict reason=slab_overflow slab_used=95% free_pages=8
2026-03-15T11:12:02Z KV shard=42 prefill=true decode=false token_count=4096
2026-03-15T11:12:03Z stream stall id=abc123 wait_for=kv_read p99=2.8s
```

sam: that looks like prefill-heavy workloads are evicting decode-hot entries -> decode queue starves -> tail latency.

ana: (from cs) two large customers reported degraded streaming quality and a restart helped temporarily. They are asking for ETA.

raj: immediate mitigation plan: 1) rollback prefill canary (disable prefill-opt) 2) increase kv slab limit on hot shards 3) add temporary eviction throttle to protect decode keys.

lee: agree. i'll take rollback. can someone prepare the config toggle and patch? ops-runner, can you patch rollout to kill prefill on canary ring?

ops-runner: deploying toggle to canary and prod-stage now: `kv.prefill.optimized=false` -> patch applied to canary ring (2026-03-15T11:18).

marta: after toggle -> canary p99 down from 2.3s to 0.9s within first 2 minutes. pushing to prod-stable next.

raj: while that happens i'm increasing slab size for the top 6 affected shards: `kvctl set-slab --shard 42,43,44 --size +20%` — doing one shard at a time.

sam: note: prefill vs decode imbalance means we should treat decode keys as high-priority non-evictable for now. can we flip policy to protect recently-decoded entries?

marta: added a soft-protect policy: `evict.policy=protect_decode_hot` on hot shards. applying now.

ops-runner: prod-stable toggle applied (11:25). metrics show prod p99 down to ~1.1s then trending lower.

raj: still seeing occasional streaming stalls in eu-west-1 p99 ~1.6s. probably cross-region warmup + fragmentation. continuing slab adjustments.

lee: FYI i opened a rollback of the prefill optimization commit with PR #8123 to formalize the revert and add guardrails.

marta: capturing customer impact: two customers impacted intermittently for ~40m, degraded streaming and longer tail (we saw increased client reconnects). CS Ana filed incident timeline.

ana: thanks — i'll notify customers with an interim note: root cause under investigation, mitigations applied, we'll follow up with RCA.

sam: logs show a surge of small queries that trigger prefill for long sequences; suspect a client-side prompt-misuse pattern. we should add per-customer prefill caps.

raj: agreed. medium-term action items: 1) per-tenant prefill caps 2) slab auto-resize policy improvements 3) make decode-hot protection permanent 4) add alert that correlates prefill evict ratio with decode queue depth.

lee: for now handing off oncall to @lee-night for overnight monitoring. leaving runbook notes: 
```
- watch grafana panels: kv-prefill-evict, decode-queue-depth, stream-p99
- if p99 > 2s in any region, rollback prefill toggle (kv.prefill.optimized=false) and increase slab on top-6 shards
- escalate to eng-sre if stalls persist >15m
```

raj: marking incident as mitigated for now. final metrics: us-west-2 p99 0.85s, eu-west-1 p99 1.02s (was 2.6s peak).

marta: i'll create an incident ticket and assign RCA to eng-ml + eng-runtime. initial hypothesis: canary prefill optimization increased hot prefix occupation causing fragmentation and evicting decode-weighted entries.

ops-runner: scheduled a rolling compaction job over kv shards at 02:00 UTC to defragment.

ana: CS will follow up with affected customers and share the mitigation steps.

lee: handoff notes: monitoring stable but not normal. leave pager awake for next 2 hours. i'll re-evaluate before wide-zone business hours.

raj: thanks everyone. i'll post follow-up with RCA draft once eng-ml and runtime finish root cause analysis. :white_check_mark:
